passages.text: After every happiness comes misery; they may be far apart or near. The more advanced the soul, the more quickly does one follow the other. What we want is neither happiness nor misery. Both make us forget our true nature; both are chains — one iron, one gold; behind both is the Atman, who knows neither happiness nor misery. These are states and states must ever change; but the nature of the Soul is bliss, peace, unchanging. We have not to get it, we have it; only wash away the dross and see it.
passages.note: Ups and downs of happiness; an unchanging peace within

passages.text: If the mind is pleased with praise, it will be displeased with blame. All pleasures of the senses or even of the mind are evanescent but within ourselves is the one true unrelated pleasure, dependent upon nothing. It is perfectly free, it is bliss.
passages.note: Hurt by criticism or hungry for praise

passages.text: Neither seek nor avoid, take what comes. It is liberty to be affected by nothing; do not merely endure, be unattached. Remember the story of the bull. A mosquito sat long on the horn of a certain bull. Then his conscience troubled him, and he said, “Mr. Bull, I have been sitting here a long time, perhaps I annoy you. I am sorry, I will go away.” But the bull replied, “Oh no, not at all! Bring your whole family and live on my horn; what can you do to me?”
passages.note: Small annoyances; not letting things get to you

passages.text: Our best work is done, our greatest influence is exerted, when we are without thought of self. All great geniuses know this.
passages.note: Doing good work; letting go of ego

passages.text: We are what our thoughts have made us; so take care of what you think. Words are secondary. Thoughts live, they travel far.
passages.note: The power of our thoughts over who we become

passages.text: Bless men when they revile you. Think how much good they are doing you; they can only hurt themselves.
passages.note: Being insulted or attacked by others

passages.text: We renounce and go on, then find nothing and despair; but hold on, hold on.
passages.note: Despair on the spiritual path; persevering

passages.text: “Be like a lily — stay in one place and expand your petals; and the bees will come of themselves.”
passages.note: Restless striving; quietly growing and letting others come
